title: Finite etale pushforward preserves constructible module sheaves
statement: Let $h:V\to U$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $G$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $V_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $h_*G$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is constructible on $U_{\Et}$ in the same finite constructible-stratification sense.

source.place: Tag 095H, label lemma-pushforward-constructible, module clause for finite coefficient rings

proof.text: Convert the given finite-module-value constructibility witness to IsConstructibleSheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. Finite products preserve this predicate: the zero sheaf has the trivial stratification, and binary biproducts are constructible by the common-refinement proof in thm-constructible-serre. Identify biproducts with binary products and use finite-product induction, including the empty product. Isomorphism invariance transports the result.

For an explicitly split finite cover with clopen coprojections i_j and isomorphisms e_j from the sheets to the base, put s_j = e_j^{-1};i_j. The two inverse identities follow from the isomorphism identities. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product]. Each factor is constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], applied directly in ModuleCat. Apply step 1 and transport along the product isomorphism.

At every point x of U choose the neighbourhood g_x:W_x -> U and splitting given by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split]. Pull G back to the fibre product; this is constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback]. Step 2 proves constructibility of its pushforward to W_x. The etale base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction], whose existing Lean theorem is generic in the coefficient category, identifies this pushforward with g_x^*(h_*G). Thus h_*G is constructible after pullback to each W_x. The chosen points prove that these neighbourhoods cover U.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings] directly to this cover of the qcqs scheme U. Obtain a finite affine covering D_b -> U and actual morphisms D_b -> W_{a(b)} over U. Pull back the witnesses from step 3 along these morphisms. The inverse-image composition isomorphism and the factorization equality give constructibility of (D_b -> U)^*(h_*G).

Let D be the coproduct of the finitely many affine D_b. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] its coprojections are an open cover. The finite coproduct is affine (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry/Limits.lean, finite-family IsAffine instance), hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Its induced map q:D -> U is surjective because the D_b cover U. For the pullback q^*(h_*G), restriction to each coprojection agrees, by inverse-image composition and Sigma.ι_desc, with the constructible sheaf of step 4.

Constructibility on a finite affine open cover implies global constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core]: replace each open immersion by its isomorphic open range, choose a constructible stratification there, and apply the theorem to obtain a global partition with actual factorization maps into the local strata. Pull their finite locally constant sheaves back along those maps; the composition isomorphisms identify the results with the global stratum restrictions. This proves q^*(h_*G) constructible. Convert back by the module-sheaf comparison and apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-surjective-pullback] to q. Both D and U are qcqs, and q is surjective, so h_*G is constructible. All empty-index cases are retained.
